sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Unicode NFKC and Zero-Width Byte Inspector Studio. Test all three Unicode traps and switch between Naive NFKC Only and Full Canonicalize with Zero-Width Stripping to see why invisible characters break SQL joins until stripped.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at Trap 1 in the inspector canvas! Even after NFKC collapses the fi ligature, that red U+200B Zero-Width Space survives untouched—and SQL join equality keeps failing until Two-Stage Zero-Width Stripping kicks in!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Checkpoint 1. A pipeline applies Python unicodedata normalize NFKC before deduplication, yet visually identical customer usernames fail equality in SQL joins. Identify the surviving character class and the exact remediation.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Check the byte sequence we just inspected in Lab 1! NFKC handles typographic ligatures and full-width digits, but skips invisible formatting controls like U+200B Zero-Width Space and Byte Order Marks!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exact diagnosis! Unicode compatibility normalization skips zero-width formatting characters like U+200B and Byte Order Marks U+FEFF because they carry bidirectional formatting roles. Composing NFKC with explicit zero-width regex stripping restores deterministic SQL join equality.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Remember that compatibility normalization folds typographic ligatures like fi and full-width numbers, yet deliberately leaves formatting control characters like U+200B zero-width space and U+FEFF intact. You must compose NFKC with an explicit zero-width regex strip.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Minimum-Cost Constraint Repair and Hot-Deck Studio. Compare raw violations, naive listwise dropping that erases 75% of the EHR ward cohort, and Bohannon Minimum Modification Repair r star paired with 1-nearest-neighbor Hot-Deck donor imputation.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Watch that cohort retention bar leap from 25% under naive deletion straight up to 100% under Bohannon Minimum Repair r star! Total weighted modification cost is only 3.0 and Patient 104 receives exact donor Age 45 from closest neighbor P_101!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2. Three clinic records share ZIP 94305 with weight 5.0: Records 1 and 3 list Stanford, while Record 2 lists Palo Alto at weight 1.0. Select the repair satisfying the functional dependency at minimum Bohannon modification cost.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Remember to sum domain attribute weights across all three valid repairs: editing Record 2's City costs 1.0, flipping two rows' Cities costs 2.0, and mutating a verified ZIP costs 5.0!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Brilliant optimization! Modifying Record 2's low-weight City attribute from Palo Alto to Stanford incurs a total Bohannon modification cost of only 1.0—strictly beating the 2.0 majority flip and the 5.0 ZIP mutation while preserving 100% of records.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect cost derivation. Let us sum the modification distance across consistent states: updating only Record 2's City to Stanford costs 1.0, flipping both Stanford rows costs 2.0, and modifying a verified ZIP key costs 5.0. Bohannon's principle selects Option A at cost 1.0.
